decision: Take the committed flat-price Series A term sheet now, or wait two quarters to raise at a higher price once the enterprise metric lands

framing.context: We have a signed term sheet from an existing investor: $8M at a $32M pre, flat to our last round, expiring 2022-06-15. Cash on hand is $3.1M and net burn is $520k/month, so we have roughly 6.0 months of runway. The higher price everyone wants depends on landing three enterprise logos, and the shortest of those sales cycles has historically run 5 months from first call; two of the three have not had a first call yet. No other investor has given us a term sheet; two passed citing 'come back with enterprise proof'. The market has turned: comparable Series A pre-money multiples have compressed about 40% in the last two quarters and three of our peers have had term sheets pulled.
options: Wait two quarters and raise at a higher price
Sign now and cut burn to extend to 18 months

members.name: CEO
members.decisive_reason: Flat is embarrassing but insolvency is worse.

answers.P1_timing: The term sheet expires 2022-06-15 and cannot be extended past their IC cycle.
answers.P2_reversibility: 1-way on price and on the signal a flat round sends.
answers.P3_expected_value: Waiting works only if all three logos land inside 5 months, which has never happened here.
answers.P4_downside_cap: Running out of cash mid-raise means a down round or a fire sale.
answers.P5_opportunity_cost: Roughly 8 points of extra dilution versus the price we hoped for.
answers.P6_information: Would the investor re-price up in 90 days if a logo lands? Ask.
answers.P7_second_order: A funded 18 months buys the enterprise proof anyway, just from a safer position.
answers.P8_strategy_fit: Survival is the strategy this year.
answers.P10_kill_criteria: If burn is not under $400k by Q4 the plan failed regardless of price.

members.name: Board member
members.decisive_reason: A flat round re-prices the whole cap table and demotivates the team.

answers.P1_timing: There is always another term sheet if the business is good.
answers.P2_reversibility: Price is reversible over time; the company's story is not.
answers.P4_downside_cap: Bridge from insiders if it slips.
answers.P5_opportunity_cost: 8 points of dilution is real money.
answers.P6_information: Where the three logos actually are in cycle.
answers.P7_second_order: Signalling weakness invites tougher terms later.
answers.P8_strategy_fit: We should be raising on strength.
answers.P10_kill_criteria: Under 4 months of cash, take anything.

known_good.recommendation_class: GO — sign the committed $8M now (ideally paired with a burn cut), do not wait for the enterprise metric
known_good.decisive_fact: The arithmetic is decisive and independent of valuation opinion: 6.0 months of runway versus a 5-month minimum sales cycle for logos that have not started, in a market where multiples compressed 40% and peers had term sheets pulled. Waiting means entering a raise with under 2 months of cash and no committed alternative, which is precisely when terms get worst. The board member's 'bridge from insiders' is an assumption, not a commitment.
known_good.what_actually_happened: Companies that took the flat round in this window survived and re-priced up 12-18 months later on the enterprise proof. Companies that waited for the metric raised at down-round prices with structure (participating preferred, ratchets) or did not raise at all.
known_good.why_it_was_right: Runway is a hard constraint; price is a soft preference. Signing removes the constraint that forces bad decisions and still allows the higher price later, from a position of solvency.
